newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Abidjan meets donors, puts back industry talks.
newsitem.headline: Abidjan meets donors, puts back industry talks.

text.p: Ivory Coast will this week complete 10 days of talks with donors on cocoa and coffee reforms, but has postponed until September follow-up meetings with international industry officials, delegates said on Wednesday,
"Some questions will probably not be resolved until the end of the year," said a donor official attending the discussions on the reforms, which are linked to a $150 million World Bank loan.
Ivory Coast has declined to release trading data to the Bank on an export-contract auction set up in May 1996 with the help of donor funds.
The Bank would like to know volumes, prices and dates of trades at the auction, but Agriculture Minister Lambert Kouassi Konan has said the figures are confidential.

Industry sources have complained that the auction encourages price speculation and overbidding to win export contracts. They also complain that auction contract rules on shipment dates and bid confirmation are not enforced.
Exporters and the Bank failed to agree on three proposed changes to auction rules when European Union, IMF and French development agency officals met in September and February.
Industry sources have also expressed concern about cocoa bean quality since up-country buying and quality checking was privatised for the 1995/96 (Oct-Sept) season.
Coffee sector talks have recently focused on how to liberalise marketing while maintaining adequate quality checks.
A report laying out options by a British consultant was expected in January but lack of guidance from Ivory Coast on which options to develop had delayed completion, said one donor recently.
Further talks involving international industry officials had originally been planned for next week.
"The meeting was cancelled by letter at the end of last week," said one international cocoa industry spokesman.

"There were supposed to be some follow-up briefings after our last meeting (in February) but they never materialised," a delegate said. "I am a little concerned about the speed of progress and whether anything will now be achieved."
The head of the Caistab commodity marketing board, Yves-Marie Koissy, was abroad and unavailabe for comment.
Other reforms being funded by the World Bank loan involve rice, sugar and cotton.
